> A custom-designed hardware timer built to eliminate smartphone distractions during deep work. It features a multi-button tactile interface and a 1.3" OLED screen that grows a digital tree over time, dying if focus is broken(timer is stopped). All study sessions automatically sync to a companion mobile app via BLE for real-time productivity tracking

## Design

### 2026-10-11: Journal Entry: Learning KiCad (DigiKey Tutorial Breakdown

**5h**

Journal Entry: Learning KiCad (DigiKey Tutorial Breakdown

To get the Lock-in Clock off the ground for my Week 1 submission, I had to figure out how to actually design a custom PCB. I started with zero experience and worked through Shawn Hymel’s 10-part "Intro to KiCad" series from DigiKey. Here is a summary(you can skip the summary its for myself anyways ) of the core concepts I learned and how I am applying them to my build:

The Design Pipeline (Part 1): I learned that building a PCB isn't just drawing lines on a grid. It follows a strict, multi-stage workflow: Schematic Capture ---> Footprint Assignment ---> Board Layout ---> Gerber Export.

Schematics & Custom Symbols (Parts 2-3): I learned how to use the Schematic Editor to map out the logical connections of my circuit. Because my focus tracker uses specific parts like the Raspberry Pi Pico W and Cherry MX switches, I also learned how to create custom schematic symbols from scratch for parts that aren't in the default library.

Physical Footprints (Parts 4-5): A schematic symbol only represents logic; the "footprint" represents the actual physical copper pads that will be manufactured on the board. I learned how to use the Footprint Editor to define those exact physical dimensions and link them back to my schematic symbols.

Board Layout & Routing (Parts 6-7): This is the main event. I learned how to use the PCB Editor to draw the "Edge Cuts" (which will define the physical rectangular shape of my macro pad) and strategically place my components. I also learned how to route the copper traces to connect the switches and OLED screen to the Pico W without crossing lines, and how to run a Design Rules Check (DRC) to catch fatal errors.

Exporting for Manufacturing (Parts 8-10): Finally, I learned how to translate my digital design into Gerber and Drill files. These are the universal blueprints used by PCB fabrication houses, and they are exactly what I will be uploading to the Half-Life dashboard for my funding review.

Also i am designing the PCB layout by myself using AI as it is not teached in this course so i have a prototype ready but a lot of changes are required

also still i am a bit inexperience so it is taking a lot of time to build stuff but atleast i built the schematic in about an hour so i am proud of that

btw , i only have one day to complete the next  5  hours  which i am curious to do and ambitious to design   , well  that's my half life experience
